bumble.name: Bumble
bumble.key_insight: Bumble proves that behavioral constraints can be more powerful than behavioral nudges. While Tinder maximizes engagement through unlimited swiping and variable-ratio matching, Bumble deliberately constrains user behavior — women must message first within 24 hours or the match expires. This constraint solves three problems simultaneously: it reduces unwanted messages for women (the #1 complaint on dating apps), it forces genuine interest signaling (matches that survive the 24-hour window have higher intent), and it creates a differentiated brand identity ('the feminist dating app'). The 24-hour expiration exploits scarcity and loss aversion — a match that's about to expire feels more valuable than one that sits indefinitely. Bumble's expansion into BFF (friend-finding) and Bizz (professional networking) using the same swipe+constraint UX reveals the strategic insight: the behavioral mechanics of dating apps are not specific to dating — they are general-purpose social sorting mechanisms. The ethical dimension is genuinely positive: Bumble's constraint design demonstrably reduces harassment compared to unconstrained platforms.
bumble.top_technique: Women-First Messaging Constraint as Power Architecture

candy-crush.name: Candy Crush
candy-crush.key_insight: Candy Crush Saga has generated over $20 billion in lifetime revenue by perfecting a single behavioral loop: give players a sense of near-mastery, then introduce failure through randomness, then offer to sell the solution. This is not accidental — it's the direct application of Natasha Schull's 'machine zone' concept from casino design to mobile gaming. The game's levels are algorithmically tuned to produce a specific failure rate: too easy and players don't spend, too hard and they quit. The optimal frustration point — where players believe they 'almost had it' and one more try (or one purchased power-up) will succeed — is the core monetization engine. The lives system (5 lives, 30-minute regeneration) creates artificial scarcity of play itself, making continued play feel like a premium commodity. King's brilliance is making the monetization feel like the player's choice ('I choose to buy a power-up') rather than the system's design ('the level was tuned to make you fail without one'). Candy Crush is the purest distillation of free-to-play behavioral economics: the product is free, and frustration is the revenue model.
candy-crush.top_technique: Near-Miss Level Design as Monetization Engine
